title: Establishability lifecycle: the same four propositions on an improved record
prepared_for: Tavares Heath — second reconstruction (v3 record), the 'after' of a before/after pair

propositions.statement: the recorded verdict RED-CONFIRMED follows the declared verdict rule (pytest_exit_code != 0 -> RED-CONFIRMED) applied to the recorded exit code (1)
propositions.basis: From the v3 record (SHA-verified): pytest_exit_code = 1; rule 'exit_code != 0 -> RED-CONFIRMED'; verdict = RED-CONFIRMED. 1 != 0 => RED-CONFIRMED. Internal consistency of the record — unchanged from run 9

propositions.statement: the recorded non-zero pytest outcome (a test genuinely failed) is corroborated by the preserved execution reports and GitHub's observed workflow behaviour, and the exact exit code is now recorded on a channel separate from the field that asserts the verdict
propositions.basis: The pytest output (hash-matched) reads '6 failed, 465 passed, 35 skipped'; the JUnit (hash-matched) carries failures='6'. STRENGTHENED since run 9: the exit code '1' is now written to its own hashed artifact (red-proof-exit-code.txt, SHA-256 4355a46b…), observable separately from the record's verdict field. GitHub's separately-hosted job steps corroborate exit_code != 0 (dependent on the same workflow execution). The run-9 limitation — the integer living only in the verdict-asserting field — is ADDRESSED, within scope: this is better artifact separation, NOT full source independence — the exit-code file and the JSON field both derive from the same workflow run and the same shell variable

propositions.statement: during run 38495005061 the intended admin-auth assertions failed with exactly the symptom the injected regression produces — admin endpoints no longer requiring authentication
propositions.basis: STRENGTHENED since run 9: the post-injection `git diff` is now CAPTURED and its SHA-256 BOUND into the record identity (injection_diff_sha256 29d73e8f…). The preserved diff RECORDS the intended code modification, and its digest is bound to the evidence record — the diff shows main.py `return verify_token(credentials)` -> `return None` at both auth points (the observed CONTENT of the modification, distinct from the event that produced it). The six failing tests are the intended auth-rejection assertions (e.g. /v1/audit returned 200, invalid token accepted) — exactly the effect of disabling token verification. The causal step from the bound modification to the failures is now strongly grounded (observed modification + matching symptom across six assertions). Reservation kept: the bound diff records the modification contemporaneously, but the hash does not by itself prove the executed code was EXACTLY the diffed code; a fully formal before/after execution proof would still be more demanding, and FactNotebook does not re-run

propositions.statement: all six IDENTIFIED admin-auth rejection assertions executed in this run failed under the injected modification
propositions.basis: ESTABLISHED — and this is the state that MOVED. In run 9 this was CANNOT ESTABLISH because pytest ran with -x and stopped at the first failure. In v3 fail-fast (-x) is removed: the run completed (506 tests; 465 passed, 6 failed, 35 skipped) and the six failing tests are all admin-auth rejection assertions — test_audit_endpoints_reject_missing_token, test_replay_rejects_missing_token, test_tenant_register_rejects_missing_token, test_tenant_delete_rejects_missing_token, test_invalid_token_rejected (TestAdminEndpointsRequireAuth), test_production_disables_auth_bypass (TestAuthEnforcement). IDENTIFICATION CRITERION for 'the relevant set': tests that assert a protected endpoint returns 401 on a missing/invalid bearer token — exactly the control the sabotage disables (verify_token -> None). What is ESTABLISHED is the NARROW proposition: these six named, executed assertions all failed under the injection (directly verifiable in the JUnit). What is NOT claimed: that these six are an EXHAUSTIVE set of every conceivable auth regression — that would require classifying the whole suite's scope, which this record does not do. The run-9 coverage limitation is addressed, within that stated scope, by evidence rather than argument. This does not change what run 9 established: it is a different run whose observations support what the earlier run's could not
